subject: Physics
description: Refraction laws, Snell, total internal reflection, lenses, optical phenomena

questions.stem: REFRACTION of light occurs because light:

options.option_text: Changes speed when entering a different medium
Bounces off the surface of medium (option here)
Gets absorbed inside the medium (option here)
Splits into colours by prism only (option here)

questions.explanation: REFRACTION = bending of light when it passes from one medium to another, due to CHANGE IN SPEED. Speed in vacuum: c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s. In water: ~2.25 × 10⁸ m/s. In glass: ~2 × 10⁸ m/s. REFRACTIVE INDEX n = c/v_medium (n_water ≈ 1.33; n_glass ≈ 1.5; n_diamond ≈ 2.42). When light enters denser medium → SLOWS + bends TOWARDS NORMAL; lighter → speeds + bends AWAY. SNELL's LAW: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. INSIGHT — refraction explains: pencil bending in water, pool depth illusion (looks shallower), lens function, mirages, RAINBOWS (refraction + reflection in raindrops, splitting white light by wavelength).

questions.stem: TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION occurs when light tries to go from:

options.option_text: Denser to lighter medium beyond critical angle
Lighter to denser medium at any angle
Vacuum into a denser medium (option here)
Same medium back to itself here (option here)

questions.explanation: TIR — when light goes from DENSER to LESS DENSE medium AT ANGLE > CRITICAL ANGLE, ALL light is reflected back into the denser medium (no refraction; refraction angle = 90° at critical angle). Critical angle θ_c: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁. For glass-air: sin θ_c = 1/1.5 → θ_c ≈ 42°. WATER-air: ~49°. APPLICATIONS: (1) FIBRE-OPTIC cables (light bouncing along glass core); (2) DIAMOND sparkle (high n → low critical angle → light trapped + multiply reflected — gives 'fire'); (3) SHEEN of MIRAGES (hot road appears reflective — air layers of varying density act as TIR boundary); (4) PRISMATIC binoculars (TIR replaces silvered mirrors — better quality). KEY exam fact.

questions.stem: A CONVEX LENS (converging) of focal length 10 cm. Object placed at 30 cm. Image is:

options.option_text: Real, inverted, smaller than object
Virtual, erect, larger than object
Real, inverted, larger than object
Virtual, erect, smaller than object

questions.explanation: Object at u = −30 cm; f = +10 cm (convex lens). Lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/10 + 1/(−30) = (3−1)/30 = 2/30 → v = 15 cm. POSITIVE v → REAL image on opposite side. Magnification m = v/u = 15/(−30) = −0.5 → INVERTED + DIMINISHED (half size). INSIGHT — for CONVEX lens: object beyond 2F → real, inverted, smaller (camera, eye); at 2F → real, inverted, same size; between F + 2F → real, inverted, larger (projector); at F → image at infinity; between F + lens → virtual, erect, larger (magnifying glass). CONCAVE lens always gives virtual, erect, smaller image (used in spectacles for myopia).

questions.stem: A pencil dipped in water APPEARS BENT. This is due to:

options.option_text: Refraction of light at water surface
Reflection of light from water alone
Diffraction of light around water
Polarization of light in water here

questions.explanation: Pencil bend illusion = REFRACTION. Light from submerged part REFRACTS at water surface (denser → lighter; bends AWAY from normal); brain projects light back in straight line → underwater part appears at different position → SHIFTED. APPARENT depth = real depth × (n₂/n₁); for water, apparent depth = real × (1/1.33) ≈ 75% real → pool seems shallower than it is. SAME REASON: stars APPEAR TWINKLING (atmospheric refraction varies with air density); SUN looks ELLIPTICAL near horizon (atmospheric refraction); fish in water look closer to surface than they are (anglers learn to compensate).

options.option_text: Concave (diverging) lens spectacles
Convex (converging) lens spectacles
Cylindrical lens used for astigmatism
Bifocal lens with two focal lengths

questions.explanation: MYOPIA — eyeball too LONG; image forms BEFORE retina. Distant objects blurry. Corrected by CONCAVE (diverging) lens — diverges incoming light, image moves back to retina. Common in students (excessive close work). HYPEROPIA / HYPERMETROPIA (long-sightedness) — opposite: eyeball too short; image forms AFTER retina; near objects blurry. Corrected by CONVEX (converging) lens. PRESBYOPIA — age-related; lens loses flexibility, can't focus near; corrected by reading glasses (convex). ASTIGMATISM — cornea irregular shape, blurry at all distances; corrected by CYLINDRICAL lens. POWER of lens (in DIOPTRES, D) = 1/f (in metres). +2 D = convex of 50 cm focal length; −2 D = concave.

questions.stem: A RAINBOW is formed due to:

options.option_text: Dispersion + reflection inside water droplets
Reflection alone from water surface
Polarization of sunlight by atmosphere
Diffraction by clouds in atmosphere

questions.explanation: RAINBOW formation: sunlight enters raindrop → REFRACTS (slows down + bends, also DISPERSES — different colours bend differently because different λ have different refractive indices); reflects off back of droplet (TIR); refracts again on exit. Result: 7 colours (VIBGYOR — Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) emerge at angles. Rainbow appears in arc on OPPOSITE side of Sun (sun behind observer). RED on outer arc; VIOLET inner. SECONDARY rainbow — fainter, larger, colours REVERSED — due to 2 internal reflections. INSIGHT — Newton's discovery that white light is composite (Opticks, 1704). Same dispersion in PRISM. SCATTERING (different): blue sky (Rayleigh — short λ scattered more); red sunset (long λ travels more horizontal atmosphere).

questions.stem: Refractive index of DIAMOND (~2.42) is one of the HIGHEST. This causes:

options.option_text: Multiple TIRs inside → dazzling 'fire'
Diamond to absorb most of the light
Diamond to scatter blue light only
Light to pass straight without bending

questions.explanation: Diamond's HIGH refractive index (~2.42) → very LOW critical angle (sin θ_c = 1/2.42 → θ_c ≈ 24.4°). Light entering diamond easily exceeds critical angle when trying to escape → undergoes TIR multiple times before finding a face to exit at low enough angle. Result: light bounces around inside, exits with high intensity → 'BRILLIANCE'. CUTTING DIAMOND with precise angles + facets (e.g., 58 facets in BRILLIANT CUT) maximises this. Also, dispersion in diamond is high → splits white light → colourful 'FIRE' or sparkle. JEWELLERY 4Cs = Cut, Clarity, Colour, Carat. DIAMOND SIMULANTS: cubic zirconia (n = 2.17, lower fire), moissanite (n = 2.65, more fire than diamond).
